A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpectralSplats and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably across additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SC4D and GART tracking experiments, quantitative comparisons, optimization demonstrations and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds global-loss comparisons, a basketball tracking experiment and further ablations.

M1.justification: The spectral-moment objective, frequency annealing, spectral-to-spatial optimization, MLP/direct deformation parameterizations and ARAP regularization are retained. The foreground-processing description documents application to the added scene without establishing a revision to the proposed tracking algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds one real-world thrown-basketball sequence from Dynamic 3D Gaussians. It tests large inter-frame motion despite correct initial alignment, extending the earlier initialization-displacement scenarios. SC4D, GART and the existing demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: V1 compares against pixel and LPIPS supervision. V2 adds Pyramid of Gaussians (PoG) and Euclidean Distance Transform (DT) to the GART comparison in Table 2 and the teaser-scene comparison in Appendix F. This substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives to include competing global objectives.

E3.justification: The added basketball experiment uses monocular, temporally subsampled inputs, aligned first-frame initialization and foreground optimization with background recomposition. Appendix C.3 adds testing with 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 frequency bands. Previously reported metrics, training budgets and main hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds frequency-band sensitivity analysis, a Shiba-specific loss-component breakdown and a case study of object merging under PoG and DT. The basketball example also examines fast motion with imperfect masks. These are targeted extensions; the original dataset-wide ablation, shift sweeps, multi-view analysis and LPIPS failure example remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing GART mean and minimum/maximum displays are retained, with no new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched SC4D and Pixel/Ours GART scores are unchanged, but substantial comparative evidence is added. Table 2 adds PoG and DT mean PSNRs of 17.0933 and 20.9199 against the retained Ours value of 22.0583, alongside per-dog LPIPS and SSIM results. V2 also adds Shiba ablation entries, frequency-sweep PSNRs, basketball tracking outcomes, global-baseline merging failures and runtime comparisons. V1 Table 3 survives unchanged as v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: New Appendix F.1 formally defines normalized foreground/background distance maps and the adapted DT baseline objective. The proposed method's mathematical development and Appendix A phase-wrapping and convergence derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about global spectral supervision, principled frequency annealing and initialization-robust tracking across deformation models. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly states the foreground-only scope and discusses obtaining scene masks. It adds interpretations of frequency-band stability and fast-motion failure through inter-frame zero overlap despite aligned initialization. The canonical-asset requirement and existing LPIPS/color-discrepancy limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds foreground separation/recomposition guidance, the DT baseline formulation and a runtime comparison of 437s versus 443s with stated 0–6% overhead. The 800 control points, 10K iterations, NVIDIA L40 hardware, original hyperparameter values and demo-code availability statement are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to ArtisanGS, PGDGS, Soft Rasterizer and OpenDR, covering segmentation guidance, reconstruction context and the new comparison objectives. The broader positioning relative to deformation models and frequency-guided optimization remains intact.

P1.justification: There is localized prose tightening, author and acknowledgment editing, and insertion of the fast-motion, annealing-ablation and global-baseline sections. The overall narrative and existing section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds basketball Figure 7, global-baseline Figure 16 and the Shiba ablation table, and expands Table 2 with PoG/DT columns. Existing figure imagery is retained; other changes mainly involve resizing, reflow, relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through relevant global-loss comparisons, an annealing sensitivity test and a real fast-motion example, while preserving the earlier evidence. The explicit foreground scope and baseline formulation also improve clarity. The overall gain is bounded: the basketball evidence is qualitative, and details such as temporal subsampling and PoG configuration remain unspecified.
